clue.text: One of three fighters is pursuing a beast

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the word is follows the other pieces

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, a beast of the field

explanation.surface: A warrior is chasing down some animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'three fighters' are Dumas's Three Musketeers; 'fighters' tempts a search for boxers or soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramis is one of the trio of swordsmen in Dumas's novel The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Unshaven and suffering from a hangover

definitions.meaning: feeling poorly after drinking too much

explanation.definitionFit: Rough describes a coarse, unshaven face and also colloquially means feeling ill, as after a night's heavy drinking.

clue.text: To tar boom is messy in this vessel

indicators.note: messy means jumbled up, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that tar on a boom makes a mess aboard their boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is messy' rearranges TOTARBOOM. 'Boom' and 'vessel' both suggest sailing, which helps hide the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorboat is a small craft driven by an engine, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Soldier dispatched to overlook lines

indicators.note: in a down answer, to overlook is to sit above, so the first piece stands over the second

parts.note: dispatched means sent off
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A soldier is sent off to watch over the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) is a crossword convention for 'lines'. The surface makes you think of lines of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a guard, a soldier posted to keep watch.

clue.text: Oh dear, one entering test must get instruction!

parts.note: tut is an exclamation of mild disapproval, like 'oh dear'

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the word one is placed inside the test

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that a student taking an exam needs to be taught first.
explanation.walkthrough: TUT is the written form of the tongue-click of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a session of teaching given by a tutor to a small group.

clue.text: The last lot of Vermouth wasn't so good? You've made a big improvement!

definitions.text: The last lot of Vermouth wasn't so good?
definitions.meaning: a pun: 'It' is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It, so the new drink tastes more like real It
an exclamation of approval when something gets better

explanation.surface: A drinker says the earlier vermouth was poor and praises the improved new batch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is old British bar shorthand for Italian (sweet) vermouth, as in the cocktail gin and It.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday exclamation of approval when something is better than before, and here also a joke about the vermouth called It.

clue.text: Peg, the royal daughter, is brought up as a modern youngster

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golfer sets the ball on

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means raised from the bottom, so the daughter's name reads upwards

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A princess is raised to be a modern young person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is brought up' turns REGAN into NAGER, placed under TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen, a youngster of the modern era.

clue.text: Dance combines Caribbean spirit with Egyptian soul

parts.note: rum is the liquor distilled in the Caribbean
in ancient Egyptian belief the ba is part of the soul

explanation.surface: A dance mixes island rum with an Egyptian spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Asleep on hammock, initially disturbed by mosquito

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of hammock is used

explanation.surface: Someone asleep in a hammock is woken by a mosquito.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes H from hammock, and 'disturbed' rearranges ASLEEPONH.
explanation.definitionFit: Anopheles is the genus of mosquito that carries malaria.

clue.text: Man given outer covering as a precaution

parts.note: Justin is a man's name
a case is a covering or casing

explanation.surface: A man is handed a protective coat to be on the safe side.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in case is an idiom meaning in readiness for a possible event.

clue.text: Animal deprived of tail makes animal noises

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of the animal goes

parts.note: the moose is a large deer

explanation.surface: A tailless beast lows like cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of tail' cuts the E from MOOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows low, so to moo is to make the sound cattle make.

clue.text: Cathedral plans embracing religious education

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: charts are maps or plans
RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A cathedral draws up plans that include religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts RE inside CHARTS. RE is the British school abbreviation for Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres in France is famous for its Gothic cathedral.

clue.text: Governor imprisoned by a revolutionary member of tribe

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held within, so the governor goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Latin American revolutionary
guv'nor or governor is slang for father, so pa

explanation.surface: A governor is jailed by a rebel from some tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Governor' is old British slang for one's father, so it gives a word for dad, not a state official.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people of the southwestern United States.

clue.text: Third note, then second note

indicators.note: then means next in order, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a mo is a moment, a short time like a second

explanation.surface: A musician names the third and then the second note of a scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' first sounds like music twice; the final 'note' is the definition, a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a brief written message or memorandum.

clue.text: Four cigarette ends on the floor — quite atrocious manners!

indicators.note: in a down answer, on the floor means at the bottom, below the anagram
atrocious means awful, so the letters of quite are mangled
Four sets how many letters come from the end of the word cigarette
ends means the tail of the word, so its last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled by cigarette butts dropped on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'atrocious' rearranges QUITE as ETIQU; 'Four ... ends' takes ETTE from cigarette, and 'on the floor' sets it below.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour in society, good conduct.

clue.text: Too impudent with series of deliveries completed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls, so an over bowled is one finished

explanation.surface: A cheeky bowler finishes an over, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold can mean forward or cheeky, so excess of it is cheekiness beyond limits.

clue.text: Getting rid of noise, is husband at home tucked away?

indicators.note: tucked away means stowed inside, so the pieces go into the noise

parts.note: a bang is a loud noise
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a husband is hiding at home to escape the racket.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'noise' as something to escape; it is the container wrapped round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to send away or expel, so it is ousting or removing.

clue.text: Almost complete" treatise before end of the interval

indicators.note: before means coming first, so the treatise precedes the last piece
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to complete is to end or finish
a tract is a short treatise

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A treatise is nearly finished just before the interval ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts END to EN; 'end of' takes the E of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is an interval between acts of a play, or music played then.

clue.text: See girl with posture advance

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
stance means posture

explanation.surface: Watch a girl with good posture step forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting us to look. To distance is to move on ahead and leave others behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To distance rivals is to outstrip them, going forward until well clear.

clue.text: Recognizes so-called scent

indicators.note: so-called says the word is as it is called or pronounced

parts.note: knows means recognizes

explanation.surface: Someone identifies a so-called fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose is the bouquet or smell of a wine, its aroma.

clue.text: Star one inscribed in holy table

indicators.note: inscribed in means written inside, so one goes into the table

parts.note: an altar is the communion table in a church
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A star figure is carved into a church altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inscribed in' puts I inside ALTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Altair is the brightest star in the constellation Aquila.

clue.text: Put a river fish in front of a cavalryman

indicators.note: in front of means placed first, so the fish leads

parts.note: huss is a fishmonger's name for dogfish

explanation.surface: Someone places a fish before a horse soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link. HUSS is a British name for dogfish sold for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a soldier of a light cavalry regiment.

clue.text: Cuttlefish very good in water

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so very good goes into the water

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
pi is slang for pious, very good

explanation.surface: A cuttlefish is thriving in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PI inside SEA. PI (pious) is a crossword convention for 'very good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the genus of cuttlefish, whose ink gives the brown pigment.

clue.text: I enjoy life without endless desire — it's unreal

indicators.note: without means outside, so the life word wraps around the desire

parts.note: to live is to enjoy life to the full

indicators.note: endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: Someone says they enjoy life free of desire, which is a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Illusive means deceptive or illusory, like a mirage.

clue.text: Quality of beauty: intrinsic to overture

indicators.note: intrinsic to means lying within, so the letters are inside the word overture

explanation.surface: An overture is said to have an inner beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertu is a love of fine art objects, or their artistic excellence.

clue.text: Prevent mugs getting knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the word is turned around

parts.note: pots are drinking vessels, like mugs

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stop the mugs being upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to hinder it or keep it from happening.

clue.text: Knights of old, each with silver embroidery

indicators.note: embroidery means fancy needlework or elaborate embellishment, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Knights from history each wear silver needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidery' rearranges EACHSILVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is French for a horseman, the old title of a mounted nobleman.

clue.text: Corrupt advertisement, outwardly respectable

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so respectable wraps around the advertisement

parts.note: decent means respectable

explanation.surface: A dishonest advert looks respectable on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means morally decayed and self-indulgent.

clue.text: Scrap not favoured for a stew

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
out means out of favour or fashion

explanation.surface: Scraps no longer wanted go into the stewpot.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a richly seasoned stew of meat and vegetables.
